messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: Dodging points / patterns
parts:
Hello everyone,

I want to produce a plot which shows the accumulation of objects in
different categories. Kind of like a bar chart but instead of bars of
different heights I want objects stacked on top of each other (see
attachement). Here is what I have so far (which highlights a few
issues with position_dodge not necessarily related to my problem):

library("ggplot2")

d = data.frame(x=round(runif(50)*10), y=1)

ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x=x, y=y), size=3, alpha=0.1)
# overplotting shows the amount of points in each x category

# what I want to obtain is something like:
dd = ddply(d, ~x, function(x) {
# create a fake y-coordinate for each point
x$nb = 1:nrow(x)/10 - 0.1
return(x)
})
ggplot(dd) + geom_point(aes(x=x, y=nb), size=5) +
scale_y_continuous("", limits=c(0,1.7), breaks=NA)
# the points are on top of each other. It looks a bit like a
histogram ... but with points. (see attachment)

# I'd like to do this without having to compute the fake-y
coordinate, and adapt the scale, and change the size of the points,
and the window size etc. so that the points look stacked on top of
each other

# so I tried dodging the points vertically
ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x=x, y=y), position = position_dodge(height=0.5))
# but that does not work
# NB: I have no idea what the error message means here

# dodging them horizontally does work
ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x=x, y=y), position = position_dodge(width=0.5))
# so I tried dodging them horizontally and echanging the coordinates
but that does not work either
ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x=y, y=x), position = position_dodge(width=0.5))
# and it's even worse when I flip the coordinates back
ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x=y, y=x), position =
position_dodge(width=0.5)) + coord_flip()

# I also tried grouping them and stacking them, which kind of works
ggplot(dd) + geom_point(aes(x=x, group=factor(nb), y=1),
position="stack", size=5) + scale_y_continuous("", breaks=NA)

# it is apparently stacking by adding increments of y
ggplot(dd) + geom_point(aes(x=x, group=factor(nb), y=1),
position="stack", size=5)
ggplot(dd) + geom_point(aes(x=x, group=factor(nb), y=0.1),
position="stack", size=5)
ggplot(dd) + geom_point(aes(x=x, group=factor(nb), y=-1),
position="stack", size=5)
# so that:
ggplot(dd) + geom_point(aes(x=x, group=factor(nb), y=0),
position="stack", size=5)
# does not work

Does anybody see how I could do that more intelligently, with
autozising of the points in particular? Would it be possible to devise
a new geom that does this?
The idea would be to produce such plots with any shape instead of the
points. For example, to present the evolution of banana sales over
time, you would produce such a plot with bananas instead of points.
That's not very scientific but in certain occasions (outreach,
presentations in schools, etc.) it is effective.

Thanks in advance. Sincerely,

JiHO

messages.subject: Re: Dodging points / patterns
parts:
> Does anybody see how I could do that more intelligently, with
> autozising of the points in particular? Would it be possible to devise
> a new geom that does this?

That would need a new grid grob - because only at the grob drawing
level do you have access to actual size on screen, and the ability to
redraw when that size changes.

Hadley

On Fri, Apr 15, 2011 at 6:45 PM, JiHO <jo.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
> On Wed, Apr 13, 2011 at 15:59, Hadley Wickham <had...@rice.edu> wrote:
>> That would need a new grid grob - because only at the grob drawing
>> level do you have access to actual size on screen, and the ability to
>> redraw when that size changes.
>
> I see that from Baptiste answer indeed. So now what I need is such a
> custom geom and a stat that makes the histogram computation and I
> would be nearly all set. I still don't see a way to get the size of
> the object at the grid level, so that I can make sure objects stack up
> on top of each other though.

I think Hadley's point was that Grid offers the possibility of
resizing grobs at drawing time, using a specific drawDetails method.
In particular, this is useful if you are resizing the window and/or
need to compute the size of the grob with respect to its drawing
context. Here, I believe that you want to alter the size of some
"points" so that a fixed number of them fits in a given distance.

A dummy illustration might be,

library(grid)

pointlessGrob <- function(n=3){
grob(n=n, cl="pointless")
}

drawDetails.pointless <- function(x, recording = FALSE){

y.space <- convertY(unit(1,"npc"), "in", TRUE)
y.quantum <- y.space/x$n
grid.points(x=unit(rep(0.5, x$n), "npc"), y=unit(seq(y.quantum/2,
length=x$n, by=y.quantum), "in"),
size = unit(y.quantum*4/3, "in"), pch=18)

}

grid.pointless <- function(...)
grid.draw(pointlessGrob(...))

grid.pointless()

HTH,

baptiste
